pr_title: Async import of the appStore packages

comments.comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully

The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.
The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

In the NextAuth authorize callback the password check is skipped whenever totpCode is non-empty, and the new backup-code branch never validates that TOTP, so a valid backup code plus any dummy totpCode value authenticates the user without the correct password.

After successful enablement the modal no longer calls onEnable and only the explicit Close button on the backup-code step invalidates viewer.me, so dismissing that step with Escape or an outside click leaves the settings page showing two-factor as disabled although the server enabled it.

The modal passes an explicit type="password" to PasswordField, and Input spreads caller props after its own visibility-controlled type, so the new show/hide toggle changes its icon but never reveals the password.

Setting tabIndex={-1} on the shared password visibility button removes the only show/hide control from keyboard navigation for every PasswordField consumer (login, signup, settings), not just the modal the change targets.

pr_title: fix: handle collective multiple host on destinationCalendar

comments.comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.

Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled

The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

evt.destinationCalendar is initialized to null when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination, so the optional-chained push of co-host destinations is a no-op and every connected co-host calendar is silently discarded for collective bookings.

The per-credential creation loop passes the full organizer-first destination array to every adapter, but Office365, Lark and the base CalDAV service still select element zero, so a second host's credential writes the event into the organizer's calendar (or fails) instead of its own.

The new conditional drops result.credentialId from every video reference even though createMeeting supplies it, and handleCancelBooking only calls deleteMeeting for references that carry a credentialId, so cancelling a booking leaves the external video meeting alive.

In the all-remaining-occurrences branch the loop still iterates only the organizer's credentials and selects each occurrence's first calendar reference, ignoring the co-host credential resolved by the new outer loop, so co-host calendar events of a recurring collective booking are never deleted.

Request-reschedule cleanup still builds its deletion map only from the requesting user's credentials keyed by provider type, so the co-host calendar events that EventManager now creates under other hosts' credentials cannot be deleted when a reschedule is requested.

pr_title: feat: convert InsightsBookingService to use Prisma.sql raw queries

comments.comment: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.

pr_title: Comprehensive workflow reminder management for booking lifecycle events

comments.comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.

When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.

The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

Non-immediate cancellation only marks the reminder row and defers the SendGrid cancellation to the 15-minute cron, but SendGrid rejects cancellations within ten minutes of send_at, so a reminder cancelled shortly before its send time is still delivered.

A single rejected SendGrid cancellation request throws out of the loop before the accumulated lazy Prisma deletes reach Promise.all, so earlier successful cancellations are never persisted and every later reminder in the batch is skipped.

pr_title: Advanced date override handling and timezone compatibility improvements

comments.comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime

Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))
When a date override matches, the availability check returns true before evaluating busy.every, so existing bookings, calendar conflicts and buffers no longer exclude slots on override dates.

The override check rejects a slot if any same-day override excludes it, treating multiple overrides on one date as an intersection instead of a union, so a schedule with two override windows (e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 14:00-17:00) loses all of its slots.

The weekly working-hours check rejects a slot when any interval for that weekday excludes it rather than requiring containment in one interval, so ordinary split-shift schedules produce no available slots.

Applying the timezone offset by extracting only hour and minute drops the date carry, so an override that crosses midnight after conversion (e.g. 22:00-23:59 UTC viewed at UTC+1) is reversed or attached to the wrong day and discarded by buildSlots.

pr_title: OAuth credential sync and app integration enhancements

comments.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

The webhook indexes appStoreMetadata with the database app slug (e.g. google-calendar) while the generated metadata is keyed by directory name (googlecalendar, office365calendar, zoomvideo), so valid installed apps are rejected with 404.

Replacing credential.key on sync leaves the invalid flag untouched, so a credential that was marked invalid stays excluded by consumers such as getCalendarsEvents even after valid replacement keys arrive.

The Webex sync path still validates the delegated response with webexRefreshedTokenSchema, which requires scope, token_type, refresh_token and refresh_token_expires_in, so the documented minimal access-token-plus-expiry response from the sync endpoint is always rejected.

The Lark sync path passes the delegated response through handleLarkError, which requires code === 0 and a nested data payload, so the flat access-token response from the sync endpoint is thrown as an error before any credential is updated.

pr_title: SMS workflow reminder retry count tracking

comments.comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).

The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

The retry-exhaustion cleanup deletes every reminder whose retryCount exceeds the limit regardless of whether it was eventually scheduled, so a reminder that succeeded on a later attempt is deleted along with the Twilio SID needed to cancel it, leaving an uncancellable SMS scheduled.

The retryCount update inside the catch block can itself reject (for example when the reminder row was deleted by a booking cancellation while the Twilio call was pending), and that rejection escapes the per-reminder error boundary and aborts processing of every remaining reminder in the batch.

pr_title: Add guest management functionality to existing bookings

comments.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

The handler rebuilds the calendar event with Booking.description, which stores the booker's additional notes, and publishes it as the event description to the calendar provider and the guest emails regardless of the event type's hideCalendarNotes setting, exposing notes that were hidden at booking time.

The reconstructed event omits team.members, and Google Calendar's updateEvent replaces the entire attendee list derived from that field, so adding a guest to a collective booking removes the other hosts from the calendar event.

The rebuilt event omits the persisted iCalUID and iCalSequence, so generateIcsString falls back to the raw booking UID with sequence zero and existing recipients receive an invitation that does not update the calendar entry created by the original invite.

updateCalendarAttendees discards the results of CalendarManager.updateEvent, which converts provider failures into success:false, so the mutation commits the new attendees and reports success even when no calendar invitation was updated.
Being an attendee grants permission to add guests even when the event type has disableGuests set, so a booked attendee can invite arbitrary additional people to an event whose host disabled guests.

pr_title: feat: add calendar cache status and actions (#22532)

comments.comment: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.
logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems

Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.
Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.

ENV_FILE="../.env" is resolved relative to the caller's working directory rather than the script's location, so running the script from the repository root edits or creates a .env file in the parent directory instead of the one the app loads.

Deleting the calendar cache only invokes the optional onChanged callback and never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars, so in the event-type Advanced tab (which passes no callback) the UI keeps showing the deleted cache's timestamp and delete action.

The cache-status lookup queries by the credential IDs shown in the UI, but delegated connections expose the synthetic ID -1 while their cache rows are keyed by the real credential ID, so delegated users never see cache status or the delete action.
